config.title: Test useFetch

intro.title: Test useFetch
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a test for a custom React hook called `useFetch` that fetches data from an API. You'll learn how to write unit tests using React Testing Library and Jest to verify that the hook correctly manages loading, error, and data states. The main technologies involved are React hooks, TypeScript, and testing utilities like `renderHook` and `act`. By the end, you'll understand how to mock API calls and assert the expected behavior of your custom hook in different scenarios.
intro.usecase: Testing custom hooks like useFetch is essential for building reliable data-driven applications. In real products, this pattern appears when dashboard widgets fetch live metrics, e-commerce filters load dynamic product data, or admin panels retrieve user information. Developers must ensure these hooks handle loading states, errors, and data updates correctly to prevent UI crashes. Proper testing guarantees that components using these hooks display accurate information and maintain responsiveness during network fluctuations.

objectives: Implement a test suite for the useFetch custom hook
Configure mock responses for different API scenarios
Manipulate test state to simulate loading, success, and error conditions
Apply assertions to verify data fetching behavior
Integrate testing utilities to mock network requests
Construct test cases that validate hook return values
Render test components that utilize the useFetch hook

steps.title: Import React, useState, useEffect, and useCallback
steps.instruction: Import React, useState, useEffect, and useCallback from 'react'.
steps.hint: Use a single import statement to bring in all four named exports from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing multiple hooks from React
import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react';

steps.expectedOutcome: The import statement is added at the top of the file, making the hooks available for use in the custom useFetch hook.
successCriteria: React, useState, useEffect, and useCallback are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some of the required hooks, but not all. Make sure to import React, useState, useEffect, and useCallback from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the useFetch custom hook
steps.instruction: Create a custom hook function named 'useFetch' that takes a URL string parameter and returns an object with data, loading, and error states.
steps.hint: Start with 'function useFetch(url: string) {' or 'const useFetch = (url: string) => {'. Inside, you'll need to define the return object structure.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState, useEffect, useCallback } from 'react';

// Create the useFetch custom hook here
steps.expectedOutcome: A useFetch function is defined with proper TypeScript typing for the URL parameter and return object.
successCriteria: The useFetch function is created with a URL string parameter and returns an object with data, loading, and error properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your useFetch function has the correct parameter type and returns an object with the required properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useFetch function isn't properly defined. Check that it takes a URL string parameter and returns an object with data, loading, and error states.

steps.title: Define TypeScript interfaces for the hook
steps.instruction: Define two TypeScript interfaces: one named FetchState<T> with data, loading, and error properties, and another named UseFetchReturn<T> that extends FetchState<T>.
steps.hint: Create interfaces with proper types: data can be T or null, loading is boolean, error is string or null.
steps.expectedOutcome: Two TypeScript interfaces are defined: FetchState<T> with data, loading, error properties and UseFetchReturn<T> that extends it.
successCriteria: Interfaces FetchState<T> and UseFetchReturn<T> are defined with correct property types.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that both interfaces are defined with proper generic types and property signatures.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interfaces aren't defined correctly. Make sure to create both FetchState<T> and UseFetchReturn<T> interfaces with the required properties.

steps.title: Initialize state in useFetch
steps.instruction: Inside the useFetch hook, initialize state variables for data, loading, and error using useState with the FetchState<T> type. Set data to null, loading to true, and error to null.
steps.hint: Use useState with the FetchState<T> generic type to create three state variables with their initial values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useFetch hook will have properly typed state variables initialized with default values.
successCriteria: useState is called with FetchState<T> type, data is null, loading is true, and error is null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure all three state variables are initialized with the correct values and types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The state initialization is incorrect. Check the types and initial values.

steps.title: Create the fetchData function
steps.instruction: Inside the useFetch hook, create an async function named fetchData that fetches data from the provided URL.
steps.hint: Use the async keyword before the function definition. The function should take no parameters and fetch from the url parameter that's already available in the hook's scope.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useFetch hook now contains an async fetchData function ready to implement fetching logic.
successCriteria: An async function named fetchData is defined inside the useFetch hook.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined an async function named fetchData inside the useFetch hook.
steps.feedbackWrong: The fetchData function is missing or not properly defined. Create an async function named fetchData inside the useFetch hook.

steps.title: Wrap fetchData in useCallback
steps.instruction: Wrap the existing fetchData function with useCallback to memoize it, making it dependent on the url parameter.
steps.hint: Use the useCallback hook you imported earlier. Pass fetchData as the first argument and [url] as the dependency array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The fetchData function is now wrapped with useCallback, which will prevent unnecessary re-creations of the function on every render unless the url changes.
successCriteria: fetchData is defined using useCallback with [url] as its dependency array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've properly wrapped fetchData with useCallback and included [url] as the dependency array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The fetchData function should be wrapped with useCallback and depend on the url parameter. Review how useCallback works with dependency arrays.

steps.title: Add useEffect to trigger fetching
steps.instruction: Inside your useFetch hook, add a useEffect hook that calls fetchData() when the component mounts or when the URL changes. Include an abort controller for cleanup.
steps.hint: Use useEffect with fetchData in its dependency array. Create an AbortController, pass its signal to fetch, and return a cleanup function that aborts.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useEffect hook is added to call fetchData on mount/URL changes, with proper cleanup using an abort controller.
successCriteria: useEffect is implemented with fetchData in its dependency array and includes an abort controller cleanup.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added useEffect, but make sure it calls fetchData and includes an abort controller for cleanup.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useEffect hook is missing or incomplete. Add it to call fetchData and handle cleanup.

steps.title: Return the hook's state object
steps.instruction: Inside the useFetch hook, return an object containing the current data, loading, and error values from your state.
steps.hint: The hook should return an object with the same properties as your FetchState interface.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useFetch hook now returns an object with data, loading, and error properties that components can use.
successCriteria: The useFetch hook returns an object containing data, loading, and error values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning an object with all three properties: data, loading, and error.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hook should return an object containing the current data, loading, and error values from state.

steps.title: Render loading, error, and data states
steps.instruction: Inside TestComponent, add conditional rendering to display loading, error, and data states based on the useFetch hook's return values.
steps.hint: Check the hook's loading, error, and data properties. Use conditional logic to render appropriate UI for each state.
steps.expectedOutcome: The TestComponent will display different UI states: a loading indicator while fetching, an error message if fetching fails, or the fetched data when successful.
successCriteria: TestComponent contains conditional rendering that checks loading, error, and data states to display appropriate content for each case.
